questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash, because its results integrate with the permission UI and file links in Claude Code.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep, so escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash, because its results integrate with the permission UI and file links in Claude Code.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep, so escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- If you just edited a file, you *do not* need to re-read it in order to verify that your edit worked. This is because the Edit/Write tools will throw an error if your change failed, and the harness you are running in already tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up to help you perform a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow, certain types of design taste or API interactions, and so on). The skills which are available to you appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one which a listed skill covers and is useful for, call this tool first — the skill's instructions then load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach. Some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one specifically by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools are announced by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

5	## Цель
6	Пересобрать библиотеку М2 в **Revit 2026** так, чтобы импосты показывали реальное сечение профилей на детальном виде, сборки несли массу и обозначение из альбома, панели — размер стекла к заказу, а в библиотеке не было лишних элементов.

8	## Решения приёмки и что из них следует
9	| Вопрос | Ответ | Что делаем |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| Q1 Импост — прямоугольник | Нужен реальный профиль на детальном виде | Для каждой сборки FSC — семейство профиля импоста (контур из DWG «Узлы 1/2 М2» и альбома М2), назначается в тип импоста (параметр «Профиль»). Прямоугольник остаётся только там, где Revit требует для Coarse |

# ТЗ: система М2 (витражи + импосты FSC) · версия 1 · 2026-10-26

Основание: аудит `_bim\audit\2026-10-26\M2.md`, решения приёмки «как есть» (`_bim\review\decisions.csv`, пакет fdddd03b… — «Вернуть» на пересборку), решения в чате 26.10.2026.

## Цель
Пересобрать библиотеку М2 в **Revit 2026** так, чтобы импосты показывали реальное сечение профилей на детальном виде, сборки несли массу и обозначение из альбома, панели — размер стекла к заказу, а в библиотеке не было лишних элементов.

## Решения приёмки и что из них следует
| Вопрос | Ответ | Что делаем |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 Импост — прямоугольник | Нужен реальный профиль на детальном виде | Для каждой сборки FSC — семейство профиля импоста (контур из DWG «Узлы 1/2 М2» и альбома М2), назначается в тип импоста (параметр «Профиль»). Прямоугольник остаётся только там, где Revit требует для Coarse |
| Q2 Толщина 62/64/64,6/65 | Разная по ситуациям — так и надо | Толщину не унифицируем. **Учесть:** есть стойки с интегрированным нащельником и стойки, где нащельник забивается — профиль и состав деталей типа должны это отражать (список — из узлов DWG и альбома, см. «Открытые вопросы») |
| Q3 ADSK_Масса, ADSK_Обозначение | Заполнить из альбома | ADSK_Масса (кг/м сборки) = Σ вес 1 п.м. детали × расход (из `profiles.csv`); ADSK_Обозначение = обозначение основания по альбому (например «FS.C-21»). Детали без веса в альбоме (уплотнители, FS.C-29) — масса помечается неполной, вопрос производству |
| Q4 Размер стекла | Добавить | Новые общие параметры экземпляра панели `FT_Стекло_Ширина`, `FT_Стекло_Высота` (мм); значения по правилам `glass_rules.csv` для пары соседних импостов, проверка `check_glass.py` |
| Q5 LOGO в контексте | Убрать | Удалить семейство «в контексте» LOGO из библиотечного RVT |

## Что меняется
| № | Что | Где | Источник | Как проверить |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Удалить LOGO | 1 экземпляр семейства «в контексте» (id 440112 в копии) | Q5 | аудит: in_place_families = 0 |
| 2 | ADSK_Масса, ADSK_Обозначение | 88 типов импостов М2 | Q3; profiles.csv (вес 1 п.м.) | 88/88 заполнено; масса = пересчёт по каталогу (fst-spec-price) |
| 3 | Параметры FT_Стекло_Ширина/Высота | панели витражей М2 | Q4; реестр параметров | параметры есть, GUID в реестре |
| 4 | Значения размера стекла | все панели витражей М2 | glass_rules.csv (рис. 43–51) | check_glass.py: FAIL = 0, NO_RULE — в вопросы |
| 5 | Семейства профилей импостов | по одному на каждый вариант сечения FSC21/22/139/144/17/18 (с учётом нащельника) | Q1, Q2; DWG «Узлы М2», альбом М2 | визуальная приёмка: сечение на плане Fine совпадает с узлом альбома |
| 6 | Назначить профили в типы импостов | 88 типов М2 | п. 5 | все типы М2 имеют профиль ≠ системный прямоугольник |
| 7 | Перевод в Revit 2026 | библиотечный RVT | решение 26.10 | файл сохранён в 2026, исходник 2017 не тронут |

## Что НЕ меняется
- Архитектура: системные витражи + импосты + двери-панели.
- Имена типов витражей и импостов, имена параметров `FT_*` и `ADSK_*` (их используют проектировщики).
- Толщины стоек по ситуациям (Q2).
- Исходные файлы bimlib 2017 в `models_files`.

## Открытые вопросы (не блокируют начало)
- Какие стойки М2 с интегрированным нащельником, а какие с забиваемым — извлекается из DWG «Узлы 1/2 М2» и альбома; спорное — производству.
- Вес уплотнителей и FS.C-29 для ADSK_Масса.
- Размер `L2` в правилах стекла (рис. 48–49).
- Цены — не входят в эту версию (нет Excel-прайса и таблицы FS.C ↔ ФСТ).

## Условия работы
- Общие параметры: ФОП проекта собирается из существующих параметров модели (точные GUID библиотеки); новые `FT_Стекло_*` — новые GUID в группе FT. Официальный ФОП ADSK (BIM2B) — для сверки, когда будет скачан.
- Экспорт PDF-листов приёмки: разрешён; профиль horizun `full_write` включает человек в Revit (панель Horizun).
- Все записи — dry-run → визуальный пакет → «Принять» → применение.

## Критерии приёмки (гейт 2)
1. Аудит «после»: критических FAIL нет, in_place_families = 0.
2. ADSK_Масса/Обозначение: 88/88, сходится с пересчётом.
3. Стекло: FAIL = 0.
4. Визуально: сечения импостов на плане Fine совпадают с узлами альбома; толщины по ситуациям сохранены; нащельники — как в узлах.
5. Спецификация ГОСТ собирается, предупреждений Revit нет.

## Объём и порядок (партии для dry-run)
1. Партия A (данные): п. 1, 2, 7 — один визуальный пакет (таблица изменений).
2. Партия B (стекло): п. 3, 4 — пакет с картинками витражей и таблицей стекла.
3. Партия C (профили): п. 5, 6 — по одной сборке FSC за раз, начиная с FSC21; пакет с сечениями.

# ТЗ: система М1 (цельностеклянный витраж, зажимной профиль) · черновик 1 · 2026-10-27

Статус: **черновик**, ждёт визуальной приёмки «как есть» и утверждения (гейт 1). Основание: аудит `_bim\audit\2026-10-27\M1.md`, решения по М2 (`tz\M2.md`).

## Цель
Сделать М1 полноценной: сейчас 4 типа импостов (у пола, у потолка, у стены левый/правый; 6 экземпляров) без единого артикула — спецификация деталей М1 пустая.

## Что меняется
| № | Что | Где | Источник | Как проверить |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Состав деталей FT_*_Артикул/Расход | 4 типа импостов М1 | альбом М1 (зажимной профиль, клипсы FS.C-145/147, крышки FS.C-151/153, уплотнители) + **подтверждение производства** | 4/4 заполнено, все артикулы в каталоге |
| 2 | ADSK_Масса, ADSK_Обозначение | 4 типа | profiles.csv (М1) | 4/4, сходится с пересчётом |
| 3 | FT_Стекло_Ширина/Высота | панели витража М1 | **в альбоме М1 правил расчёта стекла нет** (glass_rules.csv: только М2, М3) — нужны от производства | после ответа: check_glass.py FAIL = 0 |
| 4 | Профили импостов | 4 сборки | DWG «Узлы М1» (артикулов текстом нет — сверка по картинке), альбом М1 | визуально: сечение на Fine = узел |

## Что НЕ меняется
Тип витража «Система М1_Зажимной профиль_Цельностеклянное заполнение», имена типов импостов, толщина 31,4–32 мм.

# Открытые вопросы по данным производства

## 2026-10-26 — первичный разбор документов
- [ ] Нужна таблица соответствия обозначений альбомов (`FS.C-xx`, `FS.M2-xx`) и артикулов прайса (`ФСТ-xx`). Кому: производство. Почему: без неё цены не привязываются к профилям и импостам. Источник: Альбомы М1–М3 (DOCX), «Прайс Технологический 14.09.2026.pdf».
- [ ] Технологический прайс в Excel (или DOCX). Кому: производство. Почему: таблица PDF при извлечении разваливается, цены нельзя надёжно связать со строками. Источник: «Прайс Технологический 14.09.2026.pdf».
- [ ] Что такое размер `L2` в формулах стекла на стойке усиленной М2 (рис. 48–49)? Кому: производство. Источник: «Альбом технических решений М2.docx.txt»:1117, :1126.
- [ ] Обозначения для 4 комплектующих М1: «Уголок выравнивающий 723010», «Закладная в раму 40 М2 под петли», «Уголок соединительный для рамы ЦС зажимной М1-2…», «Комплект сухарей М1(М2) и М2(М2)». Кому: производство. Источник: profiles.csv.
- [ ] Вес уплотнителей и заглушек (нужен ли в спецификации массы ADSK_Масса). Кому: BIM-отдел. Источник: profiles.csv (пустой weight_kg_m).
- [ ] Каталог: FS.C-29 «Нащельник узкий примыкание» используется в модели (10 типов FSC21) и упомянут в альбоме М2 (стр. 975, 978, 1137), но не имеет таблицы профиля (вес, периметр). Кому: производство. Источник: пилот М2, catalog_check.csv.
- [x] Дубли: «Методичка по полотнам.dwg» и «Методичка по полотнам 2026.pdf» — считать одинаковыми (решение человека, 2026-10-26). **Проверено** (fst-dwg-reader, LibreDWG → DXF): артикулы 38 в DWG / 36 в PDF, различия — артефакты извлечения текста PDF (FS.C-109 подтверждён на картинке листа 2 PDF); размеры совпадают с учётом склейки чисел в PDF; единицы DWG — мм. Отчёт: `_bim\dxf\Методичка по полотнам.compare.md`.
- [ ] **Методичка по полотнам: в DWG есть листы, которых нет в PDF 2026** (проверено по картинкам листов 2, 20, 21, 28, 54, 59, 60 и по координатам в DWG):
  - FS.C-83 «Полотно Loft» — 21 вхождение на листах «Установка дверного полотна (Loft) в проем через стойку»; в PDF во всех узлах Loft M — FS.C-192 «Полотно Loft M»;
  - FS.C-104 «Рама Concept M3» — лист «Собранную раму Concept M3 зафиксировать к проему…» с полотном FS.C-103; в PDF на аналогичном листе 60 «Concept 72» — FS.C-103 + FS.C-217 «Рама (петлевая) Concept 72».
  Вероятно, DWG — рабочий файл со старыми листами (Loft → Loft M, рама Concept M3 → Concept 72), а PDF 2026 — отобранный печатный набор. **Вопрос производству:** выпускаются ли сейчас полотно FS.C-83 (Loft) и рама FS.C-104 (Concept M3)? До ответа для моделей брать состав из PDF 2026; правило «самый свежий по дате файла» здесь не применять к лишним листам DWG. Чтение текста, таблиц и состава — по PDF; точная геометрия узлов — по DWG адресно, при сборке конкретного профиля.
- [x] Дубли инструкций DV 5 и Loft M: новые версии (22.10.2026) отличаются от старых (26.09.2024) — отверстие ∅20 → ∅22, добавлены п. 10 (притвор У для двустворчатых), рис. 14, фрезеровка под шпингалеты и замок AGB 35. Ответ по правилу: канон — новые версии (Claude, 2026-10-26).
- [ ] **Узлы М3.dwg**: артикулы **FS.C-188, FS.C-216, FS.C-218** есть только в этом DWG (нет в альбоме М3, методичках, прайсе, каталоге). Что это за профили (названия, вес, к какой системе)? Вероятно, новинки (Concept 72?). Также в узлах М3 встречается FS.C-21 (стойка основная **М2**) — так и задумано? Кому: производство. Источник: `_bim\dxf\Узлы М3.compare.md`.

## 2026-10-27 — проработка систем М1, М2, М3
- [ ] **Узкая стойка М3 — какой артикул?** Модель: FS.C-09 (20 типов FSC09); альбом М3 (2024): FS.C-115 «Стойка узкая М3», вес 0,663 кг/м, формулы стекла рис. 55, 58; DWG «Методичка по полотнам»: FS.C-11 «Стойка узкая симметричная» ×4 и FS.C-09 ×1, а FS.C-11 там же подписан «Нащельник омега». До ответа в модели М3 берём **FS.C-115 из альбома** (ровно один документ с таблицей и весом) и не меняем артикул без утверждения ТЗ. Кому: производство. Источник: `_bim\inventory\M3\types.csv`, profiles.csv:76, `_bim\dxf\Методичка по полотнам.texts.txt`:16.
- [ ] **Нащельник узкий в М3:** модель использует FS.C-28 (нащельник М2), альбом М3 даёт для узкой стойки FS.C-203 «Нащельник узкий периметр». Менять на FS.C-203? Кому: производство. Источник: types.csv М3 (FSC09), profiles.csv:87.
- [ ] **М1: у 4 типов импостов все FT_*_Артикул/Расход пустые.** Состав деталей для сборок «примыкание к полу / потолку / стене левый / правый, однослойное» берём из альбома М1 (зажимной профиль, клипсы, крышки, уплотнители) — подтвердите состав и расход на 1 п.м. для каждой сборки. Кому: производство. Источник: `_bim\audit\2026-10-27\M1.md`.
- [ ] **20 артикулов из DWG, которых нет в альбомах** (`_bim\catalog\profiles_dwg.csv`, статус «новый»): для перегородок важны FS.C-09, FS.C-29, FS.C-188, FS.C-216, FS.C-218 (вопросы выше); остальные — дверные полотна и коробки (FS.C-52 SV, FS.C-66/67, FS.C-72 EG, FS.C-83 Loft, FS.C-103, FS.C-108/109 Т4, FS.C-121/122 Т5, FS.C-169, FS.C-187/201 DV, FS.C-192 Loft M, FS.C-217) — нужны для дверей: вес и актуальность. Кому: производство.
- [x] Узлы в DWG — PDF не нужны: DWG читаются fst-dwg-reader (2026-10-26); узлы М2 подтверждены альбомом М2.

content.text:
Все три системы прошли аудит по методологии, и по каждой есть ТЗ. Модель только читалась, ничего в ней не менялось. Пакеты визуальной приёмки для М1 и М3 ещё не собраны.

**Итог по системам**

| Система | Что в модели | Главная проблема | Документы |
|---|---|---|---|
| М2 | 88 типов импостов | — | [ТЗ](_bim/tz/M2.md) ждёт вашего утверждения |
| М3 | 109 типов, 320 экземпляров | у узкой стойки три разных артикула в трёх источниках: FS.C-09 / FS.C-115 / FS.C-11 | [аудит](_bim/audit/2026-10-27/M3.md), [черновик ТЗ](_bim/tz/M3.md) |
| М1 | 4 типа, 6 экземпляров | у всех типов не заполнены артикулы и расход деталей, поэтому спецификация М1 пустая; в альбоме М1 нет правил расчёта стекла | [аудит](_bim/audit/2026-10-27/M1.md), [черновик ТЗ](_bim/tz/M1.md) |

**Узкая стойка М3.** Модель использует FS.C-09. В альбоме М3 узкая стойка — FS.C-115, с весом и формулами стекла. В DWG методички она чаще подписана как FS.C-11, но тем же кодом там подписан и «Нащельник омега». Пока производство не ответит, предлагаю брать FS.C-115 из альбома. Артикул в модели без утверждённого ТЗ не меняю.

**Новые профили из DWG.** В чертежах 20 артикулов, которых нет в альбомах. Для перегородок важны пять: FS.C-09, FS.C-29, FS.C-188, FS.C-216, FS.C-218. Остальные — дверные полотна и коробки (SV, EG, Loft, DV, Т4, Т5 и другие), они понадобятся для дверей. Полный список: [profiles_dwg.csv](_bim/catalog/profiles_dwg.csv).

**Что заблокировано без ответа производства**
- М1: состав деталей и правила расчёта стекла. Без них данные М1 не заполнить.
- М3: только смена артикула узкой стойки и нащельника (FS.C-28 или FS.C-203). Масса, стекло и профили М3 от этого не зависят.

Все 13 открытых вопросов собраны в [questions.md](_bim/catalog/questions.md), общий статус — в [status.md](_bim/status.md).

**Что дальше по методологии:**
1. Вы смотрите М1 и М3 «как есть» на картинках.
2. Утверждаете ТЗ.
3. Я делаю изменения партиями, каждую сначала пробным прогоном.

По М2 можно начинать уже сейчас, как только вы утвердите ТЗ.

entries.description: Apply an explicit batch of parameter writes to elements, types or Project Information in ONE named transaction (one undo step), then RE-READ every parameter from the model after the commit and report value_written vs value_read_back â€” a difference is an explicit failure, not a warning. Targets resolve by BuiltInParameter name, shared-parameter GUID, or parameter name (ambiguity is an error). Parameter.Set() returning false is reported as a refused write, never counted. Writing to a type re-codes every instance of it: the blast radius is measured and reported. on_failure='atomic' (default) rolls the whole batch back; 'best_effort' commits what worked. The terminal transaction state is a first-class field.... Full installed contract: horizun://contract/tools

tabular_source.description: The writes come from a CSV instead of the writes array (give one or the other). The file is diffed against the model NOW: ops are generated only for cells whose reading differs (exact string comparison of the di... (full text: horizun://contract/tools)

path.description: Absolute path to the .csv (UTF-8, BOM tolerated).

key_column.description: Header column whose value finds the element. Exact, case-sensitive.

key_parameter.description: Parameter the key is matched against. Default: same name as key_column.

value_columns.description: {column: parameter} - each mapped column writes that parameter.

category.description: OST_ BuiltInCategory bounding the element sweep. Required: an unbounded sweep is not a cost to impose silently.

decimal_separator.description: DECLARED, never guessed from the file. When present, a cell that parses as a number under this separator and lands on a Double parameter is compared NUMERICALLY against the model's value converted to that parame... (full text: horizun://contract/tools)

writes.description: The batch. Each entry names ONE parameter on ONE target.

target_id.description: Element id OR type id. Omit (or set target='project_info') to write a Project Information field. Writing a type id affects every instance of that type.

target.description: Write to the document's Project Information element instead of an id.

parameter.description: A BuiltInParameter name (e.g. KEYNOTE_PARAM), a shared/project parameter GUID, or a parameter name as it reads in the UI. A name matching more than one parameter is an error, not a guess.

value.description: String | number | boolean | null. Coerced to the parameter's storage type; a value that cannot be coerced is an error naming that storage type, never a silent skip.... (full text: horizun://contract/tools)

transaction_name.description: The label of the single undo step this batch becomes.

on_failure.description: atomic: if ANY write fails, roll the whole batch back â€” nothing partial. best_effort: commit what worked and report the rest.

target_document.description: REQUIRED. Title or full path of the ACTIVE document to act on; this never switches documents.

confirmation_token.description: REQUIRED when dry_run=false: the token this exact request's dry run returned. Single-use, expiring; refused if the document or request changed.

dry_run.description: Resolve every target and parameter and report what WOULD be written. Opens no transaction.

allow_vary_between_groups.description: Call SetAllowVaryBetweenGroups(true) on project/shared parameters that do not vary yet. Without it Revit throws a modal at write time in any model with groups, which hangs the bridge. Reported as measured off the InternalDefinition, not assumed.

target_document_title.description: If given, the write aborts unless the active document's title matches. Writing to whichever model happened to be in front is how a batch lands in the wrong file.

max_rows.description: How many rows to include in the response. Totals are always exact regardless of this; truncation is reported.

idempotency_key.description: Required when the call mutates the model or session: a new UUID per deliberate change; reuse it only to retry the identical call.

"""Партия A М2: ADSK_Масса (кг/м сборки) = Σ вес 1 п.м. детали × расход; ADSK_Обозначение = артикул основания."""
import csv, sys, json
from collections import Counter
types_csv, profiles_csv, out_csv = sys.argv[1:4]
w = {}
for r in csv.DictReader(open(profiles_csv, encoding="utf-8-sig"), delimiter=";"):
    for k in ("code", "alt_code"):
        c = (r.get(k) or "").strip()
        if c and r["weight_kg_m"].strip():
            w.setdefault(c, (float(r["weight_kg_m"].replace(",", ".")), r["source"]))
parts = ["Основание", "Витраж", "Нащельник", "Рейка", "Держатель", "Заглушка", "Уплотнитель"]
rows, missing = [], Counter()
for t in csv.DictReader(open(types_csv, encoding="utf-8-sig"), delimiter=";"):
    mass, miss = 0.0, []
    for p in parts:
        code = (t.get(f"FT_{p}_Артикул") or "").strip()
        q = float((t.get(f"FT_{p}_Расход") or "0").replace(",", ".") or 0)
        if not code or q == 0:
            continue
        if code in w:
            mass += w[code][0] * q
        else:
            miss.append(f"{code}×{q:g}"); missing[code] += 1
    rows.append({"type_id": t["type_id"], "type": t["type"], "fsc": t["fsc"],
                 "ADSK_Обозначение": t["FT_Основание_Артикул"].strip(),
                 "ADSK_Масса": round(mass, 3),
                 "полнота": "полная" if not miss else "без: " + ", ".join(miss),
                 "было_Обозначение": t["ADSK_Обозначение"], "было_Масса": t["ADSK_Масса"]})

# М2 · партия A (данные) · пробный прогон 2026-10-27

ТЗ: `tz\M2.md` v1, утверждено 2026-10-27. Документ: рабочая копия `_bim\work\2026\BIMLIB_…ФристайлТехнолоджи.rvt` (Revit 2026.4, единственный открытый, снимок e35151c42db95a44). Ничего не записано.

## 1. Удалить LOGO (п. 1 ТЗ)
- Элемент 440112 «LOGO», категория «Обобщенные модели», семейство в контексте.
- Revit удалит вместе с ним 215 его внутренних элементов (эскизы и геометрия семейства в контексте). Других элементов удаление не задевает, заметок на видах нет.
- Проверка после: аудит `in_place_families = 0`; элементов в модели станет на 216 меньше.

## 2. ADSK_Обозначение и ADSK_Масса (п. 2 ТЗ)
- 88 типов импостов М2, по 2 значения = 176 записей, одна транзакция, при любой ошибке откат всего пакета.
- Значения: `adsk_values.csv` (тип, было, станет, полнота массы).
- ADSK_Обозначение = артикул основания: FSC139 → FS.C-139 (20 типов), FSC144 → FS.C-144 (4), FSC17 → FS.C-17 (13), FSC18 → FS.C-18 (6), FSC21 → FS.C-21 (25), FSC22 → FS.C-22 (20).
- ADSK_Масса, кг/м сборки = Σ (вес 1 п.м. детали из альбома × расход). Диапазон 0,565–2,628. Единица параметра — «Общие» (число без пересчёта).
- **Неполная масса:** у 79 типов не учтён уплотнитель FS.C-U5, у 10 — нащельник FS.C-29 (в альбоме нет веса). Только 9 типов посчитаны полностью. После ответа производства — пересчёт без изменения модели, кроме этого параметра.
- Было: у всех 88 типов оба параметра пустые. Параметры типа → значение получат все 324 экземпляра (236 из них — экземпляры этих же типов).
- Проверка после: horizun перечитывает каждое значение после записи; затем повторная инвентаризация М2 — 88/88 заполнено.

## 3. Перевод в Revit 2026 (п. 7 ТЗ)
Рабочая копия уже открыта в Revit 2026; формат станет 2026 при сохранении. Сохраняет человек (Ctrl+S) после применения п. 1–2. Исходник 2017 в `models_files` не трогается.

## Откат
`horizun_undo` (журнал horizun) или Ctrl+Z в Revit до сохранения.

- Значения: `adsk_values.csv` (тип, было, станет, полнота массы).
- ADSK_Обозначение = артикул основания: FSC139 → FS.C-139 (20 типов), FSC144 → FS.C-144 (4), FSC17 → FS.C-17 (13), FSC18 → FS.C-18 (6), FSC21 → FS.C-21 (25), FSC22 → FS.C-22 (20).

- Пробный прогон повторён 2026-10-27 с новыми значениями: 176 записей, 0 ошибок.

Рабочая копия уже открыта в Revit 2026; формат станет 2026 при сохранении. Сохраняет человек (Ctrl+S) после применения п. 1–2. Исходник 2017 в `models_files` не трогается.

horizun_hub.note: This bridge is the generic, organisation-neutral half: transport, safety guards and a tool surface over the Revit API. The delivery workflows built on it - model audits, classification catalogues, family homologation, pre-delivery QA - live in Horizun Hub, not in this add-in.

addin_assembly.means: the add-in assembly Revit loaded in THIS process, hashed here rather than guessed from a deployment path. A null field could not be read and is not a zero.

data_paths.why_not_localappdata: LocalApplicationData is redirected per-package under MSIX/AppContainer, and is a different folder outright under a different user or elevation context. The MCP server is launched by the MCP client and Revit is launched by the user, so the two can resolve it differently and neither is told - the server then writes jobs Revit never sees and reads a discovery directory the add-in never wrote to, and reports 'no Revit has published a bridge' with Revit running. The user profile is not package-redirected, so both halves reach one folder.
data_paths.legacy_note: State from before 0.3 is still in the old %LOCALAPPDATA% location. NOTHING READS IT - it is named here so a machine with old discovery files does not look like a machine with a broken bridge. Delete it when you are satisfied nothing is missing.

operational_controls.note: These are local machine controls shared by the ribbon and MCP server. When MCP is paused only horizun_health remains callable; central protection refuses potential writes to a workshared active document. sync_with_central_owner_granted is the owner's grant for operation=sync_with_central; that operation also needs permission_profile=full_write, and central protection wins over it.

"""Сверяет размеры стекла в модели с правилами альбомов Фристайл.

Вход:
  panels.csv  — выгрузка из модели (спецификация панелей), колонки:
                id; system; orientation (H|V); side_a; side_b; measured_mm; kind (L|L1); glass_mm
                side_a/side_b — обозначения профилей по краям (FS.C-21 …),
                measured_mm — измеренный в модели размер L или L1, glass_mm — размер стекла в модели.
  pairs.csv   — сопоставление пар профилей правилам (готовит Claude из glass_rules.csv,
                один раз подтверждается человеком визуально), колонки:
                system; orientation; side_a; side_b; k_L; k_L1; figure; source
Выход: таблица PASS/FAIL/NO_RULE в stdout и results.csv рядом с panels.csv.
Допуск по умолчанию 0,5 мм. Только локально, без сети.
  py -P -E check_glass.py panels.csv pairs.csv [допуск_мм]
"""
import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def num(v):
    v = (v or "").strip().replace(",", ".")
    return float(v) if v else None


def load_pairs(path):
    rules = {}
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f, delimiter=";"):
            key = (r["system"], r["orientation"], frozenset({r["side_a"], r["side_b"]}))
            rules[key] = r
    return rules


def main(panels_path, pairs_path, tol):
    rules = load_pairs(pairs_path)
    out, counts = [], {"PASS": 0, "FAIL": 0, "NO_RULE": 0}
    with open(panels_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for p in csv.DictReader(f, delimiter=";"):
            key = (p["system"], p["orientation"], frozenset({p["side_a"], p["side_b"]}))
            rule = rules.get(key)
            res = {"id": p["id"], "pair": f'{p["side_a"]} / {p["side_b"]}', "orientation": p["orientation"],
                   "glass_model": p["glass_mm"], "expected": "", "delta": "", "status": "NO_RULE",
                   "figure": "", "source": ""}
            if rule:
                k = num(rule["k_L"] if p["kind"] == "L" else rule["k_L1"])
                m, g = num(p["measured_mm"]), num(p["glass_mm"])
                if k is not None and m is not None and g is not None:
                    exp = m + k
                    res.update(expected=f"{exp:.1f}", delta=f"{g - exp:+.1f}",
                               status="PASS" if abs(g - exp) <= tol else "FAIL",
                               figure=rule["figure"], source=rule["source"])
            counts[res["status"]] += 1
            out.append(res)
    dst = Path(panels_path).with_name("results.csv")
    with open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(out[0].keys()) if out else ["id"], delimiter=";")
        w.writeheader(); w.writerows(out)
    for r in out:
        if r["status"] != "PASS":
            print(f'{r["status"]:7} панель {r["id"]}: {r["pair"]} {r["orientation"]} стекло {r["glass_model"]} ожидалось {r["expected"]} ({r["figure"]})')
-----

70:Система светопрозрачных перегородок FS.Model 2 не предназначена для создания наружных ограждающих конструкций, несущих конструкций зданий (за исключением кабин операторов, иных лёгких кабин и павильонов) и огнестойких преград.
71:
72:
73:Термины и определения
74:В данном документе используются следующие термины:
75:Светопрозрачная перегородка (далее СвПП): Перегородка, обеспечивающая, при необходимости, возможность визуального контакта и проникновения светового потока из одного помещения в другое. Так как в конструкции СвПП существует возможность применения непрозрачного заполнения, дополнительно используются термины «глухая» (полностью непрозрачное заполнение перегородки) и «комбинированная» перегородка.
76:Каркасная перегородка: Разновидность СвПП, конструкция которой включает в себя каркас со стойками и ригелями из системных профилей.
77:Стационарная перегородка – строительная конструкция, основной особенностью которой является крепление к существующим в помещении стенам, полу и потолку. Для установки и демонтажа перегородки необходимы специальный инструмент и квалификация.
78:Глухая перегородка (несветопрозрачная перегородка) - стационарная перегородка, в которой в качестве заполнения использованы непрозрачные материалы: листы гипсокартонные, ДСП, МДФ и т.п.
79:Остекленная перегородка - стационарная перегородка, в которой в качестве заполнения используется стекло. 
80:Существует 2 типа остекленных перегородок:
81:- одинарный витраж, в котором светопрозрачное заполнение секций выполнено в виде одинарного стекла;
82:- двойной витраж, в котором заполнение выполнено в виде двойного стекла;
83:Комбинированная перегородка - конструкция СвПП, которая включает в свой состав как глухие, так и остекленные секции.
84:Системный профиль - профиль, относящийся к конкретной системе СвПП.
85:Нормативно-техническая документация (далее НТД) - совокупность документов, обеспечивающих качество производимой продукции, а также ее соответствие всем утвержденным требованиям безопасности, условиям эксплуатации, хранения и транспортировки.

88:Основные характеристики
89:Система светопрозрачных перегородок FS.Model 2 обладает следующими характеристиками:
90:- толщина перегородки 65 мм в зависимости от применяемых декоративных элементов;
91:	- для декоративной отделки перегородок применяются алюминиевые профили, имеющие анодно-окисное или порошковое защитно-декоративное покрытие;
92:	- ориентировочные значения индекса изоляции воздушного шума (Rw) в перегородке без дверных проемов в условиях лаборатории:

109:Система перегородок FS.Model 2 может состоять из следующих типов секций:
110:глухие (несветопрозрачные);
111:светопрозрачные;
112:комбинированные.
113:
114:	В качестве светопрозрачного заполнения проемов могут использоваться стекла ГОСТ 111 толщиной 5, 6, 8 и 10 мм, которые в зависимости от проекта могут быть закаленными, тонированными в массе, оклеенными декоративными или упрочняющими пленками, а также другие светопропускающие материалы соответствующей толщины (например, сотовый поликарбонат). 
115:	В качестве глухого заполнения проемов могут использоваться листы гипсокартонные согласно ГОСТ 6266 толщиной 12,5 мм с различными видами декоративных покрытий или листы ламинированного ДСП ГОСТ 32289, МДФ толщиной 8, 10 мм различных цветов и текстур, а так же любой другой конструкционный материал толщиной 5, 6, 8, 10, 12,5 мм и весом одного кв.м не более 25 кг.
116:	В состав системы входят профили, позволяющие соединять секции под фиксированными и произвольными углами - от 90° до 270°.
117:
118:В секции перегородок могут устанавливаться двери различных типов:
119:одностворчатые и двустворчатые;
120:маятниковые;
121:из алюминиевых профилей с остеклением (в том числе со встроенными жалюзи);
122:со стеклянным заполнением и полнотелые с различными видами декоративной отделки;
123:двери сторонних производителей из дерева или аналогичных легких материалов с толщиной полотна 40 мм.
124:В остекленные секции перегородки возможна установка межрамных жалюзи.
125:	Отличительной особенностью СвПП FS.Model 2 является возможность производить монтаж конструкции после окончания процесса отделки помещений.
